summary: Clarify audit event contract and provide SIEM ingestion SQL/snippets
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Acme Payments) is preparing to onboard Redwood audit exports into their SIEM. They have requested a concise, authoritative event catalog (field-level contract) plus a small set of ready-to-run ingestion SQL/snippets and parsing examples for their SIEM (Splunk and Snowflake teams).

Impact:
- Customer cannot complete their compliance ingest verification without precise field names, types, and examples.
- Onboarding delay of 2+ weeks if they must reverse-engineer fields from raw exports.

Request details / Desired deliverables:
1) A field-level catalog (CSV or table) listing field name, type (string/ts/int/boolean), sample value, retention semantics (e.g., PII, redaction guidance), and TTL/partitioning hints.
2) Two short ingestion examples:
   - Splunk HEC mapping / props/transforms example for timestamp, tenant_id, event_type, and request_id normalization.
   - Snowflake copy into / staged file parsing SQL with a recommended target table DDL for efficient querying (partition by event_date, tenant_id).
3) One or two sample payload snippets for frequent event types (request.start, request.finish, audit.auth) in both raw JSON and a flattened CSV row to help DataOps teams.
4) Any known caveats: fields that may be absent for older logs, max string lengths, and which fields are redacted/pseudonymized.

Attachments customer provided: sample S3 manifest listing daily gzip files (s3://acme-redwood-audit/2026-03-08/*.gz). They included one gzipped sample file.

Security / Data sensitivity:
- Customer is handling transactional logs (payment-related). They require explicit notes about PII/PHI exposure and recommended redaction before SIEM indexing.
- They also asked whether event payloads contain prompt text or model output under any default logging regime.

Preferred format: single CSV for the field catalog, one .sql file with comments for Snowflake, and one Splunk props/transforms fragment.
steps_to_reproduce: N/A - onboarding/information request. Customer provided a sample S3 path and one gzipped sample of events. No bug reproduction steps.
investigation_notes:
Initial triage by Support: verified S3 sample available, confirmed files are newline-delimited JSON gz. No obvious PII in provided sample (masked emails). Eng runbook references SIEM ingestion patterns but lacks an enterprise-ready field CSV for customers. Suggested owner: Audit Exports docs + one infra PR to add example SQL.
Action items proposed:
- Docs team: prepare field catalog CSV and update Confluence, link to runbook.
- Infra/Export owners: provide Snowflake DDL and Splunk props example.
- Security SME: confirm if prompt/model-output can appear in logs by default and draft redaction guidance.
comments: 2026-03-10 | Maya Patel (Support): Received customer sample, validating format. Assigned triage owner.
2026-03-11 | Ava Thompson (Docs): I can draft the field CSV. Need confirmation on which fields are considered PII. Marking as waiting on Security SME.

2026-03-12 | Priya Singh (Security): Confirmed default exports do not include raw prompt text for production customers unless 'debug' logging enabled. We'll provide redaction guidance and a short checklist for customers to verify their export config.
2026-03-13 | Infra (SRE): We have a Snowflake DDL template (internal). Will adapt and provide a .sql with COPY INTO + file format options for gzip JSON_NEWLINE. Linking PR when ready.

2026-03-14 | Customer (Acme onboarding lead): Thank you — we would prefer examples that run without additional transforms and minimal post-processing. Please highlight any fields that might be missing from older exports.
resolution: Pending - docs and infra owners to deliver artifacts. Target deliverables: field_catalog.csv, splunk_props_transforms.conf, snowflake_ingest.sql, and a short security note. Estimated delivery: 2026-03-18.
workaround: Customer can continue manual mapping by sampling raw events and creating ad-hoc transforms; support provided a simple Python flatten script as a temporary aid (attached to ticket).
follow_up_tasks: Create field_catalog.csv and publish to Confluence
Open infra PR to add snowflake_ingest.sql to audit-export repo
Security checklist doc for redaction guidance
escalation_path: If deliverables cannot be produced by 2026-03-18, escalate to Eng Manager (Liam O'Connor) and Customer Success (Sofia Ramos).
